_doc: QUIET-DEFAULT-BUILD-1 baseline for scripts/check-default-build-quiet.py. This is ATTRIBUTED DEBT, not an approved list -- but unlike the 83-tag seed it replaces, every entry now carries a `keep` reason naming the harness code that parses it. History: VERIFY-INTEGRITY-3 measured 83 tags printing in a default build (nine repeating every 600 frames forever, four announcing switched-OFF features). QUIET-DEFAULT-BUILD-1 gated 70 of them behind MC2_DIAG_VERBOSE, taking a measured default-env mc2_10 run from 79 distinct tags / 439 diagnostic lines to 9 tags / 44 lines. The 9 that remain are load-bearing for verification itself: silencing them would blind the smoke harness, which is a worse failure than being noisy. Changing that is a harness-contract change and belongs to its own slice. The ratchet only ever tightens: gating a tag and removing it here is always correct; adding one requires a keep reason.

BUILD_FINGERPRINT v1.reason: scripts/smoke_lib/fingerprint.py parses this to prove the smoked exe matches the worktree HEAD. Silencing it disables DEPLOY_FINGERPRINT attribution -- the single strongest anti-'unverifiable work' control in the harness.

INSTR v1.reason: scripts/whatran.py and smoke_lib/gates.py parse the 'enabled:' banner to record which gates were armed for a run. smoke_lib/gates.py reports '[INSTR v1] banner absent' as a failure.

PERF v1.reason: scripts/smoke_lib/logparse.py + oracle_report.py + smoke_with_screenshots.py parse avg_fps/p50_ms/p99_ms. This is the perf regression signal.

RENDER_SNAPSHOT v3.reason: scripts/smoke_lib/oracleparse.py parses count_mismatch/pkt_mismatch (want 0) -- the static-prop snapshot oracle.

SMOKE v1.reason: scripts/run_smoke.py, smoke_lib/runner.py and run_editor_playtest_smoke.py key their pass/fail verdict off the [SMOKE v1] line; run_editor_playtest_smoke.py requires it explicitly. This IS the harness's result channel.

TGL_POOL v1.reason: scripts/smoke_lib/logparse.py counts pool_nulls from lines containing 'nulls='.

TIMING v1.reason: scripts/smoke_lib/logparse.py TIMING_RE parses event=/elapsed_ms= for load-phase timing.
